items.question: How does node2vec define the unnormalized transition probability for the next step of a biased random walk after the walk has just moved from node t to node v, and what role do the parameters p and q play?
items.gold_answer: node2vec sets the unnormalized transition probability to π_vx = α_pq(t,x) · w_vx for an edge (v,x). The bias term α_pq(t,x) depends on the shortest-path distance d_tx: it is 1/p when x is the same as t, 1 when x is adjacent to t, and 1/q when x is two hops away from t, so p and q control the walk's tendency to return, stay local, or explore outward.
items.evidence_quote: We set the unnormalized transition probability toπvx =αpq(t,x )·wvx, where αpq(t,x ) =    1 p ifdtx = 0 1 ifdtx = 1 1 q ifdtx = 2

items.question: Why does node2vec use a second-order random walk with parameters p and q instead of sampling the next node only according to the static edge weights w_vx?
items.gold_answer: Using only the static edge weights would ignore the network structure and would not let node2vec guide the search toward different kinds of neighborhoods. The second-order walk with p and q lets node2vec smoothly interpolate between BFS-like and DFS-like exploration, capturing that real networks can exhibit both homophily and structural equivalence.
items.evidence_quote: However, this does not allow us to account for the network structure and guide our search procedure to explore different types of network neighborhoods.

items.question: Under what conditions does node2vec assign α_pq(t,x) equal to 1/p, 1, or 1/q when choosing the next node x?
items.gold_answer: node2vec assigns α_pq(t,x)=1/p when x is the same node as t, meaning the walk would immediately return. It assigns α_pq(t,x)=1 when x is one hop from t, and α_pq(t,x)=1/q when x is two hops away from t.

items.question: What is the main goal of node2vec's flexible neighborhood sampling strategy, and how does it relate BFS and DFS?
items.gold_answer: The main goal is to create a flexible neighborhood sampling strategy that can smoothly interpolate between BFS and DFS. node2vec does this by using a biased random walk procedure that can explore neighborhoods in either a BFS-like or DFS-like fashion, rather than treating the two as mutually exclusive extremes.
items.evidence_quote: we design a flexible neighborhood sampling strategy which allows us to smoothly interpolate between BFS and DFS.
